transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Gupta (Redwood AE), Clara Li (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Saturn Labs), Maya Rodriguez (CTO), Liam Chen (ML Eng)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.app/sales/decks/quickstart.pdf, security pack link: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf, quickstart: https://redwood.app/quickstart, credits link: https://redwood.app/credits

Summary: quick discovery to understand Saturn Labs' ML infra, performance targets, and whether they go self-serve hosted vs Dedicated/Private. Customer interested in fast time-to-first-token and evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Samir from Redwood. Quick intros, then we'll run through what quickstart looks like, free credits, and get a sense of your constraints.
00:18 Daniel (Saturn): Hi Samir, Daniel here, head of AI, Maya is on for infra questions, and Liam will own the bench.
00:28 Clara (Redwood SE): Hey all, I'm Clara, I do performance and infra for Redwood. I'll jump into any technical bits.
00:35 Maya (Saturn): Thanks. Our main goal: we want to replace our homegrown transformer endpoint, lower latency for chat assistants and reduce per-token cost. We have a mix of cloud-hosted infra and some on-prem for PII.
01:02 Samir: Great. Are you leaning self-serve PLG API to test, or are you already thinking Dedicated / Private?
01:09 Daniel: Start PLG self-serve. Time-to-first-token matters — we want to see a demo, get credentials, and run maybe 1k requests/day as a pilot. If perf checks out, we may look at Dedicated.
01:30 Clara: Quickstart is really focused on that: free credits, SDKs, and a repo with examples that get you to first-token in minutes. We provide hosted API and can escalate to Dedicated with reserved capacity.
01:48 Liam: For the pilot, our 95th percentile target is sub-200ms for short chat prompts, and we do about 100 concurrent users at peak. Is that realistic on hosted?
02:12 Clara: It depends on the model variant and sequence length. Hosted uses smart routing and autoscaling; for consistent p95 <200ms at 100 concurrent users we'd often recommend a Dedicated pool, but for a short pilot you can test on hosted. Also caching/prefix KV cache can reduce work per request.
02:45 Maya: Quick question on security — we process some customer PII. Do you support VPC peering or on-prem options?
02:55 Samir: Yes. We have Redwood Private for VPC or on-prem deployments and Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity. For PLG/test you can use hosted with configurable retention and our SOC 2 package; for regulated data you'd look at Private with KMS/HSM integration and SAML SSO. We'll share the SOC2 doc.
03:20 Daniel: Great, please share. Also curious on pricing for Dedicated vs hosted — ballpark?
03:29 Samir: Hosted is usage-based (per-token / embeddings). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; we can provide estimates once you share expected qps and payload sizes. For initial quoting, we usually do a cost-per-token estimate then a Dedicated sizing exercise.
03:48 Clara: If you care about unit cost, quantization and batching are levers — Redwood Optimize suggests configs for your workload. We also do continuous batching and kernel selection to cut per-token compute.
04:15 Liam: On the quickstart, how long to first token? We want devs onboarded quickly.
04:22 Samir: Typical flow: sign up, get free credits, install SDK or curl, fetch API key. Time-to-first-token median is under 10 minutes with examples. We'll send the quickstart repo and CLI.
04:40 Maya: Are there rate limits on free credits?
04:45 Samir: There's a throttle to prevent abuse, but it's generous for proof-of-concept. We'll include the exact limits in the email.
04:55 Daniel: For the benchmark session — can your SE run against our sample prompts? We can provide a subset and a small dataset.
05:05 Clara: Yep. For a proper perf run we prefer a controlled benchmark: sample prompts, sequence length distribution, expected concurrency. We'll instrument latency traces and token breakdown. We'll also show token-level cost breakdown in Console.
05:30 Daniel: Any gotchas with hosted models versus open models? We use some open weights today and have internal fine-tunes.
05:39 Clara: Hosted has a model catalog; we host popular open models and some optimized variants. For custom weights, Dedicated or Private is the path. Be aware of compatibility around KV cache and quantized kernels — some very new forks need work.
06:05 Maya: On SSO, SAML + SCIM?
06:10 Samir: Yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning supported on Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports SSO for enterprise tiers; we'll share the SSO matrix in the packet.
06:28 Liam: How are logs/audit delivered? We need audit trails.
06:33 Clara: We surface request/response traces in Console; for Private we can forward logs to your SIEM, and we support encrypted audit logs.
06:45 Daniel: Competitors we're looking at are Anthropic for safety-first models and Replicate for flexible hosting. Any notable differences?
06:58 Samir: Replicate focuses on model hosting, Anthropic on safety tuned models. Our angle is production-grade inference + cost controls and consistent API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We provide rollouts, fallbacks, and routing policies so you don't manage many vendors.
07:18 Maya: Ok. For the pilot, we want to validate latency and cost — what's a realistic timeline?
07:24 Samir: If you can share prompts by Tues, Clara and I can schedule a benchmark next week. Pilot onboarding with free credits can be immediate; Dedicated sizing takes 2-3 weeks for a proper quote.
07:40 Daniel: Sounds good. One more — how do you handle PII masking and retention?
07:48 Clara: You can configure retention policies, opt-out of logging, and use customer-managed KMS in Private for encryption at rest. We'll include docs and recommended settings for PII handling.
08:05 Maya: Any SLA with Hosted?
08:10 Samir: Hosted has standard availability SLAs for paid tiers; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll include SLA summary in the packet.
08:25 Liam: For the benchmark, can you also measure tokenization overhead? Some of our prompts are heavy on system content.
08:32 Clara: Absolutely — we capture tokenization, model compute, and network overhead in our trace.
08:45 Daniel: Ok let's recap next steps.
08:50 Samir: Recap: I'll email quickstart + free credits + SOC2 and security pack. Clara will schedule the benchmark and run latency checks once you send prompts. You will share sample prompts and expected concurrency. We'll also include a Dedicated pricing estimate option.
09:06 Maya: Perfect. Thanks.
09:10 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by Monday with links.

Notes on transcription: some words may be mis-heard (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cash), product names sometimes slightly off. There's occasional crosstalk.

End of transcript.
